text:
Alex Chu: FYI — ACME sent their traffic extract. Need to turn it into a concrete reserved GPU plan + autoscale window we can sign to.
Meera Patel: paste the numbers?
Alex Chu: baseline = ~180 RPS steady (chat followups), peak bursts ~2.6k RPS for 3–6m windows, avg tokens per request = 140 (prompt+generation). Convo length varies; 20% are single-turn.
Caitlin Brooks: pricing ask: they want a committed price for the reserved pool and clarity on overage billing if bursts exceed reserved runway.
Alex Chu: quick calc: assume model = rtx-equivalent inference profile (our medium gen profile). We measure ~9k output tokens/sec per GPU for this workload shape. Effective tokens/sec need = (2.6k req * 140 tok) / (60s) = 6066 tok/s at burst. So peak is ~0.7 GPUs -> round up with headroom.
Alex Chu: but we need headroom for concurrency, KV cache cold-starts, and safety — recommend planning capacity in GPU-units not fractional.
Meera Patel: how much headroom?
Alex Chu: propose two layers: steady + burst buffer. Steady: cover baseline (180 RPS) -> tokens/sec = (180*140)/60 = 420 tok/s -> ~0.05 GPU -> 1 GPU min for redundancy. Burst buffer: sized for 99th percentile spikes: 6k tok/s -> +1 GPU. So reserved pool = 2 GPUs as minimum reserved commit.
Meera Patel: that seems low given their SLA. What about multi-tenant contention and token variance?
Alex Chu: add a safety multiply of 1.6 for variance and autoscale cooldown. So 2 * 1.6 = 3.2 -> round up to 4 GPUs reserved for the commit.
Samir Khan: can we express this as an autoscale policy instead of pure reservation? They want cost predictability for enterprise contract.
Alex Chu: hybrid recommended: commit 4 reserved GPUs (predictable monthly charge) + autoscale max = 16 GPUs for bursts. Autoscale policy: scale step = +2 GPUs, cooldown = 60s, evaluation window = 30s. Burst credits for short windows (<=6m) should allow temporary overshoot without immediate billing shock.
Caitlin Brooks: need sample numbers for legal/pricing: committed monthly = 4 GPUs * $X (we'll fill price). Worst-case on-demand delta if they hit max for 10h/month = 12 extra GPUs * 10h * on-demand rate. I will compute sheet once you give per-GPU price.
Miguel Ortiz: operational note: set sticky routing for session affinity to maintain KV cache locality. Otherwise per-request latency kills throughput. Also recommend route-level concurrency limit to protect p50 SLO.
Alex Chu: +1. Suggested routing: session-affinity TTL = 12h, cache-warm grace = 15s for recent conversations. If affinity misses, treat as cold path and route to quantized variant if latencies spike.
Meera Patel: question about model variants — do we have a quantized 7B equivalent validated for them?
Miguel Ortiz: we have a quantized 7B verified internally with ~1.8x speed-up and ~10% quality delta on their evals. Good fall-back for capacity overflow.
Samir Khan: security/compliance: ACME wants dedicated VPC + customer-managed KMS for keys and audit logs. That pushes them to Dedicated/Dedicated-Private product. Lead time for dedicated pool provisioning?
Alex Chu: Dedicated pool provisioning estimate = 7–12 business days for standard regions, add 2–4 weeks if on-prem or air-gapped. Note: reservation billing only available on Dedicated and higher.
Caitlin Brooks: need to surface two commercial options in the SOW: (A) 4-GPU reserved + autoscale overlay, (B) 8-GPU reserved (no autoscale) with higher monthly commit discount. We should show cost delta and risk.
Meera Patel: operational SLOs: target p95 generation latency < 450ms during steady, and < 700ms during 99th spike window. Can we meet that with the above config?
Miguel Ortiz: with sticky KV and 4 GPUs we meet p95 ~380ms steady. At very large spikes we fall back to quantized model which keeps p95 <700ms but may affect quality. We should add a graceful-degrade policy: route >95th percentile requests to quantized variant rather than queueing.
capacity-bot: autoscale suggestion created: {policy: "min:4,max:16,step:2,cooldown:60s,window:30s"} :gear:
Samir Khan: security questionnaire blocker: ACME's legal also asked about data residency — they want logs and traces retained in-region only. Is Dedicated Private the only way?
Alex Chu: yes for strict residency + customer KMS. Hosted can do region affinity but not strict in-region-only retention at the moment.
Caitlin Brooks: action items: 1) Alex to produce line-item sizing calc and 3 month cost scenarios (reserve 4 vs 8). 2) Eng (Miguel + Meera) to validate quantized fallback perf on their sample prompt set. 3) Sales (Caitlin + Samir) to prepare SOW options and flag lead time. I'll draft pricing sheet by EOD tomorrow.
Alex Chu: I'll attach the quick calc here in chat after lunch.
Meera Patel: thanks — if eng confirms quantized quality delta <=12% on their eval, we can recommend the hybrid commit.
Caitlin Brooks: noted for SOW.
Miguel Ortiz: started a small perf run on their sample: `run_perf --model quant7b --concurrency 32 --profile acme_sample.json` — will post numbers in thread when done.
Alex Chu: great. If perf looks good we'll offer a 2-week ramp window in the contract where autoscale is enabled and we meter usage to tune sizing.
Samir Khan: noted for legal.
capacity-bot: reminder: add ticket in "sales->capacity" with label `acme-enterprise-sizing` and due 3 business days.
Alex Chu: thanks all — will update after I upload the calc.
Meera Patel: :thumbsup:
